If I know *shivering* is what a body does when it is cold, I can figure out that *chattering* names what teeth do because of that cold. One word is the cause; the other is the effect. Look at *chattering* on page 27 as we read the sentence together."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"On page 27, Percy is *feverish* and his teeth are *chattering*. How are those two words related?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Being feverish is the cause. When you have a fever you get chills, so your teeth chatter. Chattering is the effect."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"Now shades of meaning. *Glumly* (p. 24) and *mournfully* (p. 28) both mean sadly, but the feeling is different. *Glumly* sounds like a gloomy mood, like being let down. *Mournfully* sounds deeper, like grieving a loss."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Why might Riordan choose *mournfully* on page 28 instead of *glumly*? Think about what Percy is going through."},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Mournfully is stronger. Percy is dealing with something really big, so the word makes the moment feel heavier and sadder than just being in a bad mood."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"Let's quickly glance at the other words in context: *assumed* (p. 23), *considered* (p. 24), *shimmering* (p. 25), *wrenched* and *shuddered* (p. 26), *dabbed* (p. 27). Read each sentence aloud with a partner and guess the meaning from the sentence around it."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Do not read all ten words as a list. Spend most time on the two pairs above, then give pairs about three minutes for the quick sentence check. Use the definitions in the vocabulary list to confirm guesses."},{"type":"directions","text":"Add all ten words (assumed, considered, glumly, shimmering, wrenched, shuddered, feverish, dabbed, chattering, mournfully) to your Unit Vocabulary graphic organizer. For each word write a definition in your own words. Put a star by lines that show how Percy feels."},{"type":"directions","text":"Reread pp. 23–28. Make a three-column chart: (1) What the adults say or do, with a quote and page number; (2) What Percy thinks or feels; (3) What this shows. Find at least three lines."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which lines show adults denying that Ms. Dodds ever existed?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"On page 23, Percy asks about Mrs. Dodds and people act like they don't know who she is, and the adults keep saying there was never a teacher by that name. The text shows they all say the same thing, so it feels like a pattern."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"How does Percy react when everyone denies it? Use a quote or a vocabulary word to show his feelings."},{"type":"sample-response","text":"Percy is confused and starts to doubt himself. On page 27 he is *feverish* with his teeth *chattering*, which shows how shaken he is. He saw it, but nobody will admit it happened."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Why does it matter that more than one adult says the same thing? What pattern does that build?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"It shows a pattern of adults ignoring a truth that is hard to believe. When teachers and Grover all say it, Percy has no one on his side, so he feels isolated."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"How does Riordan's narration, told through Percy's eyes, help us feel his isolation?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"We only know what Percy knows, so when everyone says he is wrong we feel as stuck and confused as he does. Words like *mournfully* show how sad he is."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"note","text":"Pages 23–28 should be checked against your edition. If students quote lines that differ slightly, accept any quote that clearly shows an adult denying or dismissing. Listen for students saying 'everybody' or 'nobody' to show the pattern."},{"type":"pulse-check","standards":["RL.6.1","RL.6.2"],"stem":"What pattern do pages 23–28 show about how adults treat Percy's account of Ms. Dodds?","choices":[{"text":"Adults deny or dismiss what Percy knows he saw, which leaves him confused and alone.","correct":true,"rationale":"This captures the pattern: several adults refuse to acknowledge Ms. Dodds, and Percy is left doubting himself."},{"text":"Adults believe Percy but are too afraid to say so in front of others.","correct":false,"rationale":"This is a believable misreading, but the adults do not show they believe him; they act as if Ms. Dodds never existed."},{"text":"Adults are worried about Percy's grades and want him to study harder.","correct":false,"rationale":"Grades are a familiar school concern, but the pages focus on denying Ms. Dodds, not on schoolwork."},{"text":"Percy decides he must have imagined everything and feels relieved.","correct":false,"rationale":"Percy is shaken, not relieved; his feverish, chattering reaction shows ongoing distress."}]},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Support students in citing lines and explaining how adults' words make Percy feel confused and isolated, using expanded noun phrases.","sayAsk":"Say: Tell your partner one line where an adult denies Ms. Dodds. Let students first discuss in a home language, then restate in English.","watchFor":"If students retell without quoting → Prompt: \"Which exact words show that?\" If students name only Percy's feelings → Prompt: \"What did the adults do or say to cause that?\" Success: student pairs a quote with a clear explanation using the frames."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: choosing lines that show denial","tryThis":"Highlight the first line on p. 23 together. Then have students scan for words like 'never,' 'no one,' and 'there is no.' Provide the frame: The adult says ___, which shows ___."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[]},{"situation":"Ready for extension: analyzing narration","tryThis":"Ask students to explain how the first-person narration shapes what readers believe about Ms. Dodds, and what would change if the narrator were an adult at school."}]}]},{"id":"lia-summary-central-idea","title":"Part B: Summarize and Link to a Central Idea","minutes":15,"standards":["RL.6.2","RL.6.1","RL.6.3","RL.6.5"],"routine":"Quick Write","blocks":[{"type":"text-reference","title":"The Lightning Thief","pages":"pp. 23–28"},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"A summary tells the key events in your own words, in order, and leaves out what you think or feel about them. Compare two sentences. Opinion: 'It's unfair and I hate how the adults act.' Summary: 'Percy asks about Ms. Dodds, and the adults and Grover act as if she never existed.' Only the second is a summary."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which of these is a summary sentence, and which is an opinion? 'Percy is wrong to trust Grover.' 'Grover tells Percy that there was never a Ms. Dodds.'"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"The first is an opinion because it judges Percy. The second is a summary because it tells what Grover says without adding my feelings."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"teach","text":"A central idea is the big point the details build. Our details show adults denying and dismissing Percy. So one central idea is that people who tell the truth can be doubted and dismissed, and that this can leave them isolated. Your summary should lead to that idea."},{"type":"paragraph","audience":"shared","text":"*Model:* In pages 23–28, Percy asks about Ms. Dodds, but the adults and Grover act as if she never existed. Percy feels confused, shaky, and alone because no one will confirm what he saw. These events develop the central idea that being doubted and dismissed can make a person feel isolated, even when they know the truth."},{"type":"directions","text":"Write a 3–4 sentence summary of pages 23–28 in your own words, with no opinion words like 'I think' or 'unfair.' Then add one sentence that begins 'This develops the central idea that...' and use at least two vocabulary words."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"How does your summary show a central idea rather than just a list of events?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"My last sentence connects the events to a bigger point: when adults ignore the truth, Percy is left feeling isolated. That ties all the details together."},{"type":"teacher-note","variant":"tip","text":"Circulate and look for opinion words. Ask students to swap them for what the text shows. Have two students read summaries aloud and let the class name the central idea they hear."},{"type":"eld-panel","purpose":"Support students in writing a summary distinct from opinion and linking it to a central idea with precise noun phrases and academic connectors.","sayAsk":"Provide frames: First, ___. Then, ___. As a result, Percy feels ___. This develops the central idea that ___. Expand noun phrases: *the adults* → *the adults who deny the truth*; *Percy's feeling* → *Percy's lonely, shaky confusion*. Allow students to rehearse orally with a partner, or to draft collaboratively in writing (ELD.PI.6.2) before writing alone.","watchFor":"If students include 'I think' or 'unfair' → Prompt: \"Rewrite it to tell only what the text says.\" If students list events without a bigger point → Prompt: \"What do all these details show about how Percy is treated?\" Success: summary is in own words, free of opinion, and ends with a central idea."},{"type":"support-table","rows":[{"situation":"Struggling with: separating summary from opinion","tryThis":"Give a two-column sort: 'What happened' and 'What I feel.' Have students move each sentence to the correct column, then write only from the first column."},{"situation":"Ready for extension: central idea","tryThis":"Ask students to compare this section with the museum scene from Lesson 6 and explain how the new details deepen the central idea of being doubted and dismissed."}]}]}]},{"kind":"look-back","title":"Look Back","purpose":"Students reflect on how their summary connects to a central idea and how it will help them in the performance task.","activities":[{"id":"lookback-reflection","title":"Complete the Summary Frame","minutes":5,"standards":["RL.6.2"],"routine":"Reflection","blocks":[{"type":"teacher-script","move":"say","text":"In the performance task you will summarize parts of texts and link them to big ideas. Today you practiced that with Chapter 2."},{"type":"directions","text":"Complete the frame: In pages 23–28, the adults ___. Percy feels ___ because ___. This deepens the central idea that ___."},{"type":"sample-response","text":"In pages 23–28, the adults act as if Ms. Dodds never existed. Percy feels confused and alone because no one believes him. This deepens the central idea that being doubted and dismissed can make a person feel isolated."},{"type":"teacher-script","move":"ask","text":"Which vocabulary word helped you describe Percy's feelings most precisely?"},{"type":"sample-response","text":"*Feverish*, because it shows how shaken Percy is, not just that he is upset."}]}]},{"kind":"homework","title":"Homework","purpose":"Optional reading to prepare for Lesson 8.","activities":[{"id":"homework-ch3","title":"Read and Annotate Chapter 3","minutes":0,"standards":["RL.6.1"],"routine":"Annotation","blocks":[{"type":"directions","text":"Read and annotate *The Lightning Thief* Chapter 3 (pp. 29–36).
